why: `data/programs/glyph.tokens.json` declares kuhul.glyph-token-contract.v1 — a 1024-slot vocabulary in which a glyph is an executable token carrying an id, an opcode, a phase or fold marker, and the micronaut that runs it — and `data/host/manifests/atomic-exec-glyph-lane.json` declares the frozen container those tokens travel in. Nothing in the repository read or validated either file, so the phase ladder could be renumbered, a fold token could point at the wrong phase, a dual glyph could lose a pole, or the display string could quietly become the authority, all without a single test failing.

vocabulary.law: the ranges partition the vocabulary exactly: no overlap, no gap, and every token id lies inside the range that names it

phase_ladder.law: phase k sits at id 16+k and angle 60k degrees; the ladder is the executable form of the C6 order

fold_ladder.law: one fold token per phase, in ladder order, and each token's declared phase must match its name

dual_glyph.law: a dual glyph has exactly two distinct poles, opposed in orientation, and a boundary strictly inside (0, 1)

glyph_chars.law: the character table and the fold table must agree; a character that disagrees with its fold token is refused

runtime_contract.law: execution reads token ids; the rendered glyph is a best-effort reverse lookup, so no consumer may decide behaviour from the display string

language_encoding.default_legacy: crc32 over the utf8 word, masked, modulo 894, offset 128
language_encoding.utf8_glyph: raw utf8 bytes offset by 128; declared reversible and training-required
language_encoding.law: the legacy mapping is a best-effort frequency map and is not reversible; only the utf8_glyph encoding may be called reversible

container.invariant: single-face container; semantic consumers are downstream and hold no parallel authority
container.law: unpacking a container grants nothing: it carries glyphs, it does not authorize their execution

invariants.GS1: the declared ranges partition the vocabulary exactly — no overlap, no gap, full coverage of [0, vocab_size), and every token id inside the range that names it
invariants.GS2: there are exactly six phase tokens, in C6 order, with ids 16..21, opcodes 0x01..0x06, angles 60k degrees, and a named micronaut each
invariants.GS3: there are exactly six fold tokens, ids 22..27, opcodes 0x07..0x0C, and each token's phase matches the phase its glyph names
invariants.GS4: a dual glyph carries exactly two distinct poles, opposed in orientation (upright/inverted, 0/180 degrees), with a boundary strictly inside (0, 1)
invariants.GS5: the glyph_chars table agrees with the fold token table; a character that disagrees is refused
invariants.GS6: token ids and opcodes are unique across the whole contract, including dual poles
invariants.GS7: token ids are authoritative and display strings are best-effort; a contract claiming display authority is refused
invariants.GS8: an unknown language token has the declared placeholder shape (<sNNN>), so an unidentified word is never silently mapped to a glyph
invariants.GS9: the atomic exec container is frozen, single-face, ASXG/1, and confers no authority: semantic consumers are downstream and unpacking grants nothing
